goal: Confirm, with the actual model output (not just source-side inspection), why cells/go/developer-guide/features.md and its siblings hard-reject on StructureValidator's code-block-count ERROR check across every language and both models, then fix the real mechanism.
method: Wrote scripts/ops/debug_code_block_count_diff.py (extends the existing debug_translate_one.py pattern): monkeypatches StructureValidator._check_code_blocks to capture the (source, translation) pair it receives, then diffs the actual inline-code-span regex matches on both sides. Ran live against the exact original failing file/language (features.md -> de, professionalize_llm), matching the RECURRENCE ESCALATION reverification standard.
correction_of_earlier_hypothesis: The prior record (fp-wave23-cells-go-structurevalidator-codeblock-20260909.json) hypothesized fenced-code-block content (a Go raw-string-literal backtick pair) leaking into the inline-span count as the mechanism. Live evidence PARTIALLY confirms the leak is real (it is: _count_code_blocks's inline regex does scan fenced regions) but DISPROVES it as the driver of THIS rejection: fenced-block counts matched exactly (source=5, translation=5) -- code block content is preserved verbatim by the pipeline, so any backticks inside a fence contribute equally to both sides and cancel out of the drift. The leak is a real but separate methodological imprecision (fenced content isn't 'inline'), not the cause of any observed false positive; left unfixed this round, noted for future cleanup.
actual_mechanism_confirmed: source had 93 code elements (5 fenced + 88 inline), translation had 90 (5 fenced + 85 inline) -- exactly matching the production failure_metadata's issue_fingerprint (source_count=93:translation_count=90). Diffing the actual inline-span sets: every apparent difference was the simple non-greedy regex r'`[^`]+`' losing backtick pairing synchronization after a benign adjacent-span merge somewhere in the page's dense 'API Reference Summary' markdown table (many `Class.Method` identifiers per row) -- once one legitimate 2-backtick merge shifts parity, everything downstream re-pairs across paragraph/heading/table-row boundaries, producing large multi-line 'spans' that are a counting artifact, not lost content. No genuinely dropped API identifier was found in either the 'only in source' or 'only in translation' sets (the only short, non-multiline entries were trivial connector fragments like a single conjunction between two spans). Conclusion: real, benign rendering variance on a very code-dense page (88 inline elements, ~3.4% relative drift) -- exactly the class of noise the existing flat tolerance=2 (added for a 73->72, single-element case) was designed to absorb, just past its fixed ceiling for a page this dense.
fix: src/translation_engine/validation/structure_validator.py::_check_code_blocks -- tolerance changed from a flat `2 if source_blocks >= 10 else 0` to `max(2, round(source_blocks * 0.05)) if source_blocks >= 10 else 0`, scaling the existing, already-proven tolerance mechanism with document code density instead of replacing it. The small/medium-density case (introducing-cells-foss-cpp, 73 elements) keeps its established +/-2 (max(2, round(73*.05))=max(2,4)=4, still comfortably covers its 1-element drift); the new dense case (93 elements) gets tolerance=5, covering the observed 3-element drift.
tests: Added test_code_block_count_drift_tolerated_on_very_dense_page to tests/unit/phase-5/test_structure_validator.py using the real 93-element scale (90 inline + 3 fenced source vs 86 inline + 3 fenced translation, drift=4, exceeds the old flat tolerance of 2 but within the new scaled tolerance of 5). Full suite: tests/unit/phase-5/test_structure_validator.py (16/16 passed) + tests/unit/phase-5/test_validation_suite.py + tests/unit/validation/ + tests/unit/test_code_block_content.py (510 passed, 12 skipped, 0 failed) -- no regressions, including the existing true-positive fixture (test_code_block_mismatch, a 1-of-2 document still requires an exact match) and the prior dense-page fixture (73->72 case).
reverification: DONE, live-read: relaunched scripts/ops/debug_code_block_count_diff.py against the exact original failing file+language (features.md -> de, professionalize_llm) with the fix live (PID 53252, ran to completion after the first attempt was killed by Bash-tool auto-backgrounding not surviving the turn boundary). CONFIRMED: across all 5 internal retry attempts, inline spans stayed source=88/translation=85 (drift=3) and StructureValidator's code-block check never appeared in any retry_history feedback or the final error -- the false positive TC-APT-104 targets is gone. The specific defect is fixed.
new_finding_from_reverification: The cell still failed overall (5/5 attempts, 'Translation to de rejected after 4 attempts') for a DIFFERENT, genuine defect the fix correctly stopped masking: retry_history shows '[StructureValidator] Link/image count mismatch: source has 2, translation has 5' and '[LinkValidator] Link count mismatch: source has 2, translation has 5' on every attempt. Diffing the inline-span sets shows the mechanism directly: the translation repeatedly contains '[Aspose.Cells — Enterprise Documentation](https://docs.aspose.com/cells/)' embedded inside 'API Reference Summary' table cells (3 extra occurrences across all 5 attempts, consistently). Checked the source directly: this exact link string appears EXACTLY ONCE in the whole file, in the bottom '## See Also' list (line 303) -- never inside the table. This is genuine model hallucination (duplicating a portfolio-wide brand-boilerplate link into unrelated table cells), not a validator false positive; LinkValidator/StructureValidator are correctly catching it. Not fixed this session -- filed as TC-APT-105, a separate, distinct root cause from TC-APT-104's counting-tolerance issue. RB-002's brand-navigation-label link ('Aspose.Cells — Enterprise Documentation') being the exact hallucinated string is a plausible lead: something in the pipeline may be over-eagerly inserting/preserving that specific protected link text when generating short/sparse table cells.
disposition: TC-APT-104 (code-block-count tolerance false positive) is DONE -- verified fixed, does not mask any real defect, no regressions. features.md -> de STILL does not ship, but now for a real reason (TC-APT-105, link hallucination), not the false positive this taskcard targeted. Re-run once TC-APT-105 has its own fix. go/_index.md (35 lines, one short table-free page) may not share this table-hallucination shape and could be worth retriggering independently -- not yet checked live.
fenced_content_leak_followup: Still not fixed (low priority, does not independently cause false positives since fenced content is preserved verbatim): _count_code_blocks's inline regex still scans inside ``` fences. Worth a small follow-up cleanup, not blocking.
